A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VidMuse and the V2M dataset. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original V2M-bench comparisons, model and input ablations, and a 40-participant A/B user study in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds VidMuse results on three additional benchmarks, a retrained comparator, encoder timing measurements, and dataset composition analyses.

M1.justification: The overall architecture, fusion equation, training loss, and sliding-window inference are retained. However, Section 4.1 changes the long-term and short-term branches from self-attention to cross-attention, while v3 Figure 3 still depicts a Self-Attention Block. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an architectural change or a wording error.

E1.justification: v3 Table 2 adds actual evaluation on AIST++, LORIS, and TikTok, extending the V2M-bench evaluation to additional video populations and beat-alignment scenarios, including dance videos. The finer V2M genre breakdown and new music annotations characterize existing data; they do not establish additional training-domain coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds M2UGen*, retrained using the authors' dataset. New Table 2 includes D2M-GAN and CDCD comparisons, plus V2Meow on AIST++ and LORIS on the LORIS benchmark. The qualitative comparison also adds Video2Music. These expand actual comparator participation beyond citations; the PDFs do not establish that all external baselines were rerun.

E3.justification: v3 introduces beat-based evaluation metrics and reports training-set overlap removal for the additional benchmarks. It adds encoder latency and throughput protocols using 30-second videos on H800 hardware with batch sizes 1 and 16. Section 5.1 also revises the stated training batch from 240 samples to 5 per GPU, specifying 64 pretraining and 32 finetuning GPUs. These disclosures do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 removes the entire 455M/1.9B/3.3B model-size ablation from v2 Table 4. It adds encoder timing analysis, music-genre/instrument/mood composition analyses, and a Video2Music spectrogram case. Design-choice ablations lose coverage and ImageBind results, and encoder ablations lose FD. The input, codebook-pattern, and finetuning-data ablations remain unchanged after matching their reordered appendix tables.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.2 and Table 2 introduce CSD and HSD, described as standard deviations of beat coverage and hit scores, including values for VidMuse. This adds score-dispersion reporting. Neither version documents repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new deviations do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds cross-benchmark results, the M2UGen* row, timing measurements, and dataset-analysis findings. VidMuse's new F1 scores are 98.2, 95.9, and 87.7 on AIST++, LORIS, and TikTok; results are mixed across metrics, with TikTok BCS 79.8 versus CDCD's 91.8. Model-size and selected ablation results are removed, and reported finetuning-set duration changes from 6,000 to 600 hours. Original main-comparison scores, user-study outcomes, and the three retained appendix ablation tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The fusion formulation, cross-entropy objective, Average Rank definition, and mathematical description of sliding-window inference are retained. No new or revised theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: a large and diverse 360K-pair V2M dataset, video-only generation using local and global visual cues, and superior quality, diversity, and alignment on V2M-bench. The added experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit cross-benchmark generalization and no-overfitting interpretations in Section 5.3, and newly interprets the finetuning ablation as validating ImageBind-based ranking in Section 8. Qualitative analysis extends the MIDI high-frequency limitation to Video2Music. The limitations replace the computational-resource concern with restricted input conditioning and remove the explicit 32 kHz restriction while retaining codec reconstruction concerns.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 32-frame global sampling, separate pretraining/finetuning GPU counts, 56K/8K steps and 50/8-hour durations, ViT-B encoder backbones, timing procedures, and Qwen2-Audio metadata annotation. It removes the explicit default 1.9B decoder specification, float16 statement, and several implementation-resource links. The abstract changes code/data access from a promised repository release to stated availability through a project page; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including LORIS, CDCD, Panda-70M, and further video/music research, and replaces the source-separation citation with Hybrid Transformers for Music Source Separation. References such as DETR, BLIP-2, and the original FAD paper disappear. Dataset motivation adds the problem of divergent benchmark metrics, but the main novelty positioning and related-work organization remain stable.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the main section sequence remain close to v2. Local revisions correct cross-references and rename Pretraining Effect to Finetuning Effect, remove the separate method discussion, move qualitative analysis into the supplement, reorganize appendix sections, and add acknowledgments and short supplementary explanations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the video-genre pie chart with a finer bar chart, and merges and redraws v2 Figures 3–4 as Figure 3. It adds a benchmark table and three dataset-analysis plots, removes the subset-statistics and model-size tables, reshapes ablation tables, and expands the spectrogram comparison with Video2Music. The user-study heatmaps retain their results while their presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmarks and dataset-retrained M2UGen comparator improve assessment beyond the authors' own benchmark, while hardware/timing disclosures and music-specific dataset analyses improve transparency. These gains are limited by underspecified external-benchmark procedures, removal of model-size and alignment-ablation evidence, and the new self-attention/cross-attention inconsistency. The unchanged original results and these tradeoffs support a limited overall improvement.
